kanban-claude 0.4.0.dev1

Every card the daemon dispatches is a paid claude -p session. This release makes those sessions measurable and visible. It records what each run did and cost, serves a read-only web dashboard for the board and its logs, keeps cards and GitHub issues in step, and trims the turns that workers waste.

Release explainer, 2026-10-20. Diff v0.3.0 (d2fb178) to 94d91e5 on feature/v0.4.0. This is a pre-release. The diff ends at 94d91e5. The version bump to 0.4.0.dev1 (b7d7b93) comes after it and is not part of the diff this page covers.

  • 51

    CLI verbs, up from 48: gate, github and web are new

  • v7

    database schema, up from v5: migration 6 for run measures, migration 7 for GitHub

  • 10

    worker verbs, up from 9; gate is the new one

  • +113

    test functions, 91 of them in three new files (counted with grep; the full suite passes, exit 0)

  • 13

    commits changing 50 files, +7,618 and −81 lines

Background

Why this release exists

The board now runs real work every day, and each run costs money. Four asks followed. More statistics about what runs cost and do. A view of the board in the browser. Access to every card's logs, with all the parameters of each run. And GitHub Issues and Projects kept in step with the board, the way Jira already is.

A token-efficiency plan that was already approved rode along: shorter worker prompts, a way to run long gates without flooding the worker's context, and cards that name their files. The measurements added here are what lets that plan be judged.

Read the page in this order: the map shows where each piece sits, the dashboard section shows what kanban web looks like with invented data, and the walkthrough takes one change at a time with the code behind it.

Component map

What changed, and where it sits

  • + added
  • ~ changed
  • = left as it was

Reading the arrows: the runner starts the worker and feeds every stream event to Measure, which writes the database. The runner and the worker write files into the kanban home. kanban stats and kanban web read the database, and kanban web also reads logs and prompts from the files. The GitHub sync talks to GitHub through gh api and to the database in both directions. Not drawn: kanban stats --backfill, which feeds the saved stream files through Measure.

Dashboard

What kanban web shows

Run kanban web and open http://127.0.0.1:8742/. The two pictures below are mock-ups drawn for this page. They use the real page's layout, labels and colour logic, but every card title, id and number in them is invented. Nothing comes from a real board. The real page is dark first and follows your system setting for light, as these do.

Board

One lane per status. A card shows its id, title, role, priority, pull request, model and cost. A card with a live run glows and has a line sweeping across its top edge. The dock under the lanes has a tab for each running card and follows its transcript.

Card drawer

Clicking a card opens a drawer with five tabs. Parameters shows the card's settings, then one block per run: model, effort, advisor, permission mode, tokens, the command line (with the prompt shown as <prompt>), the allow-listed environment, what the session loaded, and what the run used. Logs shows a run as a transcript or as the raw log, with filters, search, a Follow switch for live runs, and downloads for the stream, the log and the prompt. Overview, Runs and Comments hold the card's text, its run history and its thread.

Stats

A second page charts spend per day and per role, tokens by model, the advisor arms, how runs ended, the cards with the most review rounds, and the most used skills, MCP servers, tools and subagents. When some runs have no counts yet it offers kanban stats --backfill. On a database still at schema 5 the board and drawer work, and Stats shows a notice instead.

Walkthrough

Change by change

Each change says what it is, why it exists, and how you notice it. Every excerpt is cut from the tree at 94d91e5 and labelled with its file and lines.

Every run is measured +added

What changed

A new module, measure.py, reads each event of a run's stream as it arrives and keeps counts: turns, tool calls, skills, MCP servers, subagents, hooks (ok and failed), compactions, permission denials, tool errors, and how the run ended. It also keeps cache writes split by their one-hour and five-minute lifetimes, the number of advisor calls, and API time. When the run ends, the runner stores the counts as new columns on task_runs (schema 6), in the same transaction as the result.

The same pass records the run's parameters: the command line with the prompt replaced by <prompt>, ten allow-listed environment variables, and what the session reported loading at start (tools, skills, plugins, MCP servers, agents). The prompt itself is kept beside the log as run-N.prompt.md, readable only by you (mode 0600).

Why
A total cost does not say why a card was expensive. To tune prompts or roles you need counts per run: how many turns, which tools, how much was cached.
How you notice it
kanban show --json carries two new keys, harness and params. The dashboard's Parameters tab and kanban stats read the same columns.

Limit
Counting is best-effort by design. A fault inside the counter prints a traceback and the run goes on, and record_measure is guarded in Runner.finish(), so a measurement error never costs a run its recorded result. init_params takes an init event of any shape, and backfill skips a run it cannot measure and fills the rest. The environment list is an allow-list so that a variable added later cannot leak into the record by accident.

Token totals were too low, and are now summed over every model !fixed

What changed

The token columns held only the usage of the last turn in the final result. Cost came from a different field, so it was right while the token numbers were not. They now add up the run's per-model usage (modelUsage), which also covers subagent and advisor models. The schema 6 migration rewrites existing rows from the model_usage already stored with each run.

Why
Nothing looked broken, because cost and tokens sat side by side and only one was right. The token columns undercounted by orders of magnitude while the cost was right, so no total looked wrong on its own.
How you notice it
After the upgrade, kanban runs and kanban stats show token totals orders of magnitude higher than before. That is the correction, not a regression.
In the code

plugins/kanban-claude/runtime/src/kanban_claude/store.py:163-170

-- the token columns were the last result's per-turn usage; the run's `model_usage` delta covers the
-- whole run, subagent and advisor models included
UPDATE task_runs SET
  input_tokens = (SELECT COALESCE(SUM(json_extract(j.value, '$.inputTokens')), 0) FROM json_each(model_usage) j),
  output_tokens = (SELECT COALESCE(SUM(json_extract(j.value, '$.outputTokens')), 0) FROM json_each(model_usage) j),
  cache_write_tokens = (SELECT COALESCE(SUM(json_extract(j.value, '$.cacheCreationInputTokens')), 0) FROM json_each(model_usage) j),
  cache_read_tokens = (SELECT COALESCE(SUM(json_extract(j.value, '$.cacheReadInputTokens')), 0) FROM json_each(model_usage) j)
WHERE model_usage IS NOT NULL;
Limit
Only rows that have model_usage are rewritten. A row without it keeps its old numbers.

kanban stats reports roles, models and first-pass rate +added~changed

What changed

kanban stats gains runtime by role (runs, total, average, longest, API time), cost per role and model, the advisor arms, the warden first-pass rate, and cost per approved card. The first-pass rate is the share of reviewed cards whose first verdict was an approval. Cost per approved card is the sum of every run of the cards that got an approving review, so send-backs and retries are in it. It also ranks the skills, MCP servers, tools and subagents that runs used.

Runs from before 0.4.0 have no counts. kanban stats --backfill replays the saved stream files through the same counter, in batches of 50, and prints backfill: filled N runs, skipped M (no stream sidecar). A run whose stream was not kept stays unmeasured, and stats says how many.

Why
The first question after a month of use is where the money went. These tables answer it by role and by model rather than by total.
How you notice it
Run kanban stats after the backfill. Backfilled runs are marked advisor inherit, because no earlier run recorded an arm.

An advisor policy per role +added

What changed

A new config key advisor.<role> exists for smith, designer, scout, warden and atlassian. Its values are inherit (the default), off and ab. off sets CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_ADVISOR_TOOL=1 for that role's runs. ab splits cards by a hash of the role and the card id: a card keeps its arm when it is rerun, and because the role is part of the hash, smith's and warden's arms on one card are independent.

What a run records is a different set of values: inherit, on or off, plus the number of advisor calls it made.

Why
Whether the advisor earns its cost is only answerable by comparing runs with and without it on comparable cards. ab makes that split without anyone choosing which cards get which.
How you notice it
kanban config set advisor.smith ab, then read the advisor arms in kanban stats or the Advisor line of a run's Parameters.
In the code

plugins/kanban-claude/runtime/src/kanban_claude/runner.py:118-127

def advisor_arm(conn: sqlite3.Connection, run: Row) -> str:
    """D1: the advisor arm of this run, `inherit`, `on` or `off`, from `advisor.<role>`. An `ab`
    role is split by a stable hash of role and card (salted, so smith's and warden's arms on one
    card are independent, and a card keeps its arm across reruns)."""
    key = f"advisor.{run['role']}"
    policy = store.cfg(conn, key) if key in store.DEFAULTS else "inherit"
    if policy != "ab":
        return str(policy)
    digest = hashlib.sha256(f"{run['role']}:{run['task_id']}".encode()).digest()
    return "off" if digest[0] & 1 else "on"
Limit
The rule is a stable half of that role's cards, hashed from the role and the card id, so a card keeps its arm across runs and the arms of different roles on one card are independent.

kanban gate keeps long test output out of the worker's context +added

What changed

A new worker-only verb, kanban gate [--lines N] -- CMD, runs a command and writes its whole output to run-N.gate-K.log under the card's run directory in the kanban home, never in the worktree, where it would end up in the pull request. It then prints one header line (exit code, seconds, line count, log path) and a digest of at most 40 lines, or N. The digest streams the log line by line instead of reading it whole. The digest puts lines that look like failures first (FAIL, Error, error:, failed, Traceback, AssertionError), each once and at most half the budget, then --- last lines ---, then the tail where test runners print their summary.

It exits with the command's own code, or 127 if the command cannot start. A single argument runs under bash -o pipefail -c; several arguments run as an argv. An owner who runs it gets exit 5, like every other worker verb.

Why
Every line a worker reads is read again on each later turn. A 2,000-line test run costs tokens many times over, while the digest costs a few dozen lines once, and the log keeps the evidence.
How you notice it
smith, designer, warden, kanban-code-review and simplify-code-card now run their long gates through it. The Gate: line in a pull request still names the real command, not the wrapper.
In the code

plugins/kanban-claude/runtime/src/kanban_claude/worker.py:176-188

def gate_digest(lines: Iterable[str], limit: int) -> tuple[int, list[str]]:
    """The line count of a gate's output and at most `limit` lines of it: the failure-looking ones
    first (once each, in order, half the budget at most), then the tail, which is where test runners
    print their summary. Streams the lines, so a huge log never sits in memory."""
    cap, bad, last, n = limit - limit // 2, dict[str, None](), deque[str](maxlen=limit), 0
    for x in lines:
        n += 1
        if len(bad) < cap and GATE_RE.search(x):
            bad.setdefault(x)
        last.append(x)
    room = limit - len(bad) - (1 if bad else 0)
    tail = [x for x in list(last)[-room:] if x not in bad] if room > 0 else []
    return n, [*bad, *(["--- last lines ---"] if bad and tail else []), *tail][:limit]

Leaner prompts, and cards that name their files ~changed

What changed

The shared worker rules gain a turn-rules paragraph: batch independent reads, grep -n and then read line ranges, never re-read a file just written, run gates with kanban gate -- '<cmd>', and stop when the acceptance criteria are met. The designer takes one cropped screenshot per check and uses a page snapshot for structure. The scout stops once each part of its answer has a primary source.

Cards change too. The card template, the kanban skill and the card-checker now ask for a Files to touch: line of absolute paths (new marks a new file) and the exact gate and acceptance commands. The card-checker flags and fills in what is missing.

Why
A worker that has to search for the files and guess the gate spends its first turns on discovery, and every one of those turns is re-read later.
How you notice it
There is no flag. You see it in the cards the checker returns and, over a few days, in turns and tokens per role in kanban stats.
Limit
This is prompt guidance, not enforcement. Whether it saves anything is something the new stats can show, not something this page can claim.

kanban web is a separate, read-only process +added

What changed

kanban web [--port N] [--board SLUG] [--open] starts a foreground process on http://127.0.0.1:8742/; Ctrl-C stops it. The web board that 0.2.0.dev8 removed lived inside the daemon and guarded itself with a web.secret. This one has no secret, no write path and no place in the daemon. What keeps it read-only:

  • Each request opens the database read-only (mode=ro plus PRAGMA query_only) and closes it again. It never creates the file and never migrates it.
  • web is registered as a long-running verb, so the CLI path that opens and migrates the live database is never taken.
  • It binds 127.0.0.1 only, with address reuse off so it cannot sit beside a wildcard listener on the same port.
  • Only GET and HEAD are answered. POST, PUT, DELETE, PATCH and OPTIONS get 405.
  • A Host header other than 127.0.0.1:PORT or localhost:PORT gets 403, which stops DNS rebinding.
  • Log, stream and prompt files are found through a run's row, and the resolved path must lie under the kanban home. Nothing takes a path from the URL.
  • Responses carry a strict Content-Security-Policy (default-src 'self', so no inline script or style), nosniff, no-referrer and no-store. Text goes through the same terminal-escape stripping as the CLI.
Why
A server on localhost can be reached by other pages in your browser, and by a hostname rebound to 127.0.0.1. The Host check, the GET-only rule and the absence of any write path leave such a page nothing to change and nothing to read.
How you notice it
It prints kanban web 0.4.0.dev1: read-only board at http://127.0.0.1:8742/ (Ctrl-C stops). --port takes 0 to 65535, --board opens straight onto that board, and --open opens your browser. A database still on schema 5 works too, except for the Stats page.
In the code

plugins/kanban-claude/runtime/src/kanban_claude/web.py:67-79

@contextlib.contextmanager
def reader(home: Path) -> Iterator[sqlite3.Connection]:
    """A fresh read-only connection; the file is never created and its schema never touched."""
    db = home / "kanban.db"
    if not db.is_file():
        raise Error(f"no board database at {db}; is KANBAN_HOME right?")
    conn = sqlite3.connect(f"{db.as_uri()}?mode=ro", uri=True, timeout=10)
    conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
    conn.execute("PRAGMA query_only = 1")
    try:
        yield conn
    finally:
        conn.close()

plugins/kanban-claude/runtime/src/kanban_claude/web.py:722-725

    def serve(self, head: bool) -> None:
        if self.headers.get("Host") not in self.server.allowed:
            self.close_connection = True
            return self.deny(403, "unexpected Host header", head)

plugins/kanban-claude/runtime/src/kanban_claude/web.py:716-720

    def refuse_method(self) -> None:
        self.close_connection = True
        self.deny(405, "read-only: GET and HEAD only", extra={"Allow": "GET, HEAD"})

    do_POST = do_PUT = do_DELETE = do_PATCH = do_OPTIONS = refuse_method
Limit
There is no login. Anything on the machine that can reach 127.0.0.1:8742 can read the board and every log, so on a shared machine that includes other accounts. The server runs a thread per request (daemon threads), which is ordinary for a single-user local tool.

A board can follow a GitHub repository +added

What changed

kanban boards edit SLUG --github-repo [HOST/]OWNER/REPO pairs a board with a repository, optionally narrowed by --github-query and tied to a Projects v2 board with --github-project OWNER/NUMBER. A board pairs with Jira or GitHub, not both. The daemon then runs one pass every github.poll_s seconds (120 by default): export, pull, push, apply. Every GitHub call goes through gh api, outside any database transaction, and each link is applied in one BEGIN IMMEDIATE through the same functions the owner's verbs use, as the actor github.

Who owns what, as the code decides it:

  • Text. Title and body are compared field by field with what each side held at the last sync. If GitHub changed, its text is pulled, and an edit the card also had is kept as a conflict comment. If only the card changed, it is pushed.
  • Done. Read from the issue's open or closed state, and only from that.
  • Status. The card's status picks the Projects v2 Status option (github.status_map) and is never read back, because changing a Status does not bump the issue's updated_at.
  • Closing an issue on a triage, todo, ready or blocked card marks it done. On a running or review card, or when a todo child waits on it, it raises a conflict for you instead. Reopening a done or archived card sends it to triage.
  • Push guard. Before a PATCH that carries text, push() reads the issue again. If its updated_at changed during the pass, it skips the PATCH and records the link error issue changed in GitHub during the pass; merged on the next one. The next pass merges GitHub's edit, with the card's text kept in a [github] conflict comment. Comments still go out.
  • Failures. One failing link or card no longer ends a sync pass; a pause (Paused) still does.
  • Comments. Your comments cross, plus the closing text of each work run and each review verdict. The worker's own comments and [run] lines never do.
Why
It follows the Jira sync's model: either side may be edited, no text is lost, and a worker is never changed under its feet. A running card keeps GitHub's text out until the next pass.
How you notice it
Issues carrying the label kanban-claude (github.label) appear as triage cards. A linked card tells its worker to put Closes OWNER/REPO#N in the pull request body, so the merge closes the issue.
In the code

plugins/kanban-claude/runtime/src/kanban_claude/github.py:325-341

def merge_text(t: Row, lk: Row, issue: Issue) -> Merge:
    """Each side is compared with what it held at the last sync: GitHub with the read-back, the card
    with its own text then."""
    m = Merge({}, {}, {}, {})
    for col in ("title", "body"):
        card, theirs = t[col], issue.get(col) or ""
        card_edited = norm(card) != lk[f"card_{col}"]
        if norm(theirs) != lk[f"base_{col}"]:
            if norm(card) == norm(theirs):
                m.agree[col] = norm(theirs)
            else:
                m.pull[col] = theirs
                if card_edited:
                    m.lost[col] = card
        elif card_edited:
            m.push[col] = card
    return m
Limit
Nothing in this diff shows a run against a live repository. The tests use a fake gh (tests/fake_gh.py). The pass runs inside the daemon's housekeeping tick, so one slow gh call (60 seconds at most) can delay the other housekeeping jobs by that long; the code notes a separate thread as the fix if it shows up.

GitHub verbs, pauses, doctor, and the first-pass export +added

What changed

Five owner verbs: kanban github import ISSUE [--board B], link ID ISSUE, unlink ID, sync [--board B] and status. ISSUE is 12, OWNER/REPO#12 or a URL. When you link an existing card, GitHub's text wins field by field and the card's goes into a conflict comment. sync prints <board>: synced and exits 1 while the board is paused.

An authentication, rate-limit or network error pauses that board's sync until a pass succeeds; dispatching never notices. A github.lock file stops two syncs from running at once. kanban doctor gets check 21, GitHub pairing: gh authentication per host, the project scope for boards with a project (the fix it prints is gh auth refresh -h HOST -s project), and with a probe, a read of the repo and the project. It warns while a sync is paused, and says not checked while the database is below the current schema, pointing at check 5.

Why
GitHub being down or unauthorised must not stop cards from running, so the sync fails on its own and says so.
How you notice it
A repository that GitHub shows as private or internal (GitHub Enterprise) gets the first-pass export: every card that is not done or archived, has no link and was never unlinked becomes a new issue with the label kanban-claude, so a board that already holds a backlog opens a burst of issues at once. A marker makes a lost answer adopt the issue by title rather than create a second one. A public repository, or one whose visibility GitHub does not report, gets no export, because a created issue cannot be unpublished; its issues are still imported and synced. kanban github status then prints EXPORT OFF: OWNER/REPO is public; cards are not exported to it, and --json carries export_skipped.

Upgrade notes

Moving from 0.3.0 to 0.4.0.dev1

  1. Run /kanban-claude:setup between cards. Schemas 6 and 7 arrive together: the first command you run afterwards migrates the database after taking a backup. The 0.3.0 daemon then refuses it with database schema 7 is newer than this kanban, so the daemon has to be the new one before cards run again.
  2. Run kanban stats --backfill once. It fills older runs from their saved streams. A run whose stream was not kept stays unmeasured. Token totals will jump, because the old columns were wrong (see the token change above).
  3. Optional: kanban web opens the dashboard on http://127.0.0.1:8742/.
  4. Optional: pair a board with kanban boards edit SLUG --github-repo OWNER/REPO. If the repository is private or internal, the first pass exports every open card that has no link as a new issue labelled kanban-claude, so expect a burst of issues if the board holds a backlog. A public repository, or one whose visibility GitHub does not report, gets no export; its issues are still imported. Run kanban doctor first: check 21 tells you if gh lacks the project scope.
  5. Optional: kanban config set advisor.smith ab starts the advisor comparison for one role.

Quiz

Check what you took from this page

Seven questions. Pick an answer to see the explanation.

1. Why can kanban web be left running next to the daemon?

reader() opens the file with mode=ro and query_only, refuse_method answers 405, and serve() returns 403 for an unexpected Host. It is a separate process with no secret.

2. What does kanban config set advisor.smith ab do?

advisor_arm hashes role:task_id with sha256 and uses the lowest bit of the first byte. The run then records on or off; ab itself is only a config value.

3. A worker runs kanban gate -- 'pytest -q' and the tests print 2,000 lines. What reaches the worker?

gate_digest caps the digest at 40 lines by default (--lines N changes it) and the full output goes to a log file created with mode 0600, outside the worktree.

4. Before 0.4.0, stats showed the right cost but token counts that were far too low. Why?

The schema 6 migration sums inputTokens, outputTokens and both cache fields over the run's stored model_usage, and new runs are summed the same way.

5. An issue is closed on GitHub while its card is running. What does the sync do?

plan_status treats a closed issue on a running or review card as a conflict. Only triage, todo, ready and blocked cards are marked done by a close.

6. You have upgraded from 0.3.0. What do you do?

The first new command migrates to schema 7 after a backup, and a 0.3.0 daemon then refuses the database (database schema 7 is newer than this kanban). The backfill fills runs from their saved streams.

7. You pair a board that holds 30 open, unlinked cards with an empty repository that GitHub reports as private. What does the first sync pass do?

export() creates an issue for every card that is not done or archived, has no link and was never unlinked, but sync_board runs it only when is_public is false. A public repository, or one that does not report its visibility, is skipped: kanban github status prints EXPORT OFF and --json carries export_skipped. Its issues are still imported and synced, and import takes only labelled issues.
